conventions.commits: Conventional Commits (e.g. 'feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)'), signed with `git commit -S --signoff` (GPG plus DCO Signed-off-by), per CONTRIBUTING.md.
conventions.testing: Unit tests in #[cfg(test)] mod tests inside each languages/*.rs file (parse helper, then Query::new and cursor matches; e.g. java.rs test_java_element_query_happy_path); registry tests in mod.rs and lang.rs; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ using common::call_tool_raw and tempfile::NamedTempFile.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity; SPDX header check in CI; workspace deny lints undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; .github/scripts/check-package-age.sh; jscpd duplicate check; markdownlint on README.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option<String> or Vec<String>; text extraction is bounds-checked via get_node_text or an explicit end_byte <= source.len() check; no unwrap/expect outside tests; SemanticExtractor returns empty Vec on missing defuse query.

patterns: Java and Swift handlers define the five query constants plus extract_inheritance; swift.rs extract_inheritance walks children by kind when no field name exists.
Element extraction is capture-name driven: @function on the declaration node plus @method_name or @func_name, and @class on the type node plus @class_name or @type_name (parser_elements.rs:282-292).
extract_inheritance is invoked only for nodes captured as @class (parser_elements.rs:398), so interface, trait and enum captures also reach the handler.
Calls are collected from captures named exactly 'call' (parser_elements.rs:495-497); the call node text is the callee name.
Imports: import_query captures named 'import_path' feed extract_imports_from_node; unknown node kinds fall back to raw node text.
DEFUSE_QUERY capture names follow the write.* / writeread.* / read.* convention shared by Java, Swift, C#, TS, Rust and JS handlers.
css.rs and yaml.rs show the minimal handler shape with None for optional slots.

constraints: Issue #1864 states external pull requests are not accepted; the maintainers implement it in-house, so this report is research only.
supported_languages() must include "php"; QUERY_CACHE is built from it and get_compiled_queries returns UnsupportedLanguage otherwise (parser.rs:191-225).
CSS and YAML are absent from supported_languages() while present in get_ts_language and EXTENSION_MAP; this inconsistency is observed in lang.rs and parser.rs and was not traced further.
Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) so that mixed HTML/PHP files parse; this is required by the issue's HTML-template criterion.
New Cargo.lock entries must be at least 7 days old per AGENTS.md; SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK exists only as a bypass.
Workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used outside tests; undocumented unsafe is denied.
The issue excludes trait use resolution, property/constant extraction, attributes, namespace alias resolution, and .phtml/.inc/.module/.php5 extensions.
Tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 runtime depends only on tree-sitter-language 0.1, which matches the locked tree-sitter-language 0.1.9; the locked tree-sitter is 0.27.2.
test_coverage: Languages with inline unit tests include java.rs (6 test functions, grep-verified) and css.rs (3 test functions, grep-verified); kotlin.rs and go.rs also carry multiple inline tests (exact counts not tallied). mod.rs covers known, unknown and table-driven registry metadata; lang.rs covers extension lookup and case-insensitivity. parser.rs has lazy-compilation tests that use supported_languages(). Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ cover analyze tools with temp files, but no grep hit showed a PHP or Swift case, so PHP would be the first. No test currently asserts that every EXTENSION_MAP language is also in supported_languages().

approaches.name: A: Full Java/Swift-style handler with LANGUAGE_PHP (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum declarations), CALL_QUERY (function, member, nullsafe member, scoped calls), IMPORT_QUERY on namespace_use_clause, DEFUSE_QUERY (assignment/update/variable reads), REFERENCE_QUERY None in v1, and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP so HTML templates parse. Set extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type to None (issue: no consumer since #1807). Wire php in lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages) and mod.rs (mod, get_language_info, get_ts_language).
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in the issue, including the HTML-template edge case and inheritance on interfaces/enums
Mirrors the Swift (#1742) and Java integration shape, so review cost is low
LANGUAGE_PHP covers both pure PHP and mixed templates without preprocessing
cons: Requires adding 'php' to supported_languages() or QUERY_CACHE lookups fail with UnsupportedLanguage
Import text is the namespace_use_clause text, so group-use prefixes (use A\{B, C}) lose the prefix
defuse query is approximate: PHP has no local declaration node, so the first assignment is the write site

approaches.name: B: Minimal handler (element, call, import only)
approaches.description: Same as A but DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance are None; only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY are populated.
pros: Smallest diff; fewer grammar assumptions to verify
cons: Violates the issue's acceptance criteria for inheritance (extends/implements) and the DEFUSE_QUERY requirement
analyze_file would show classes with empty inherits, so the integration is incomplete

approaches.name: C: PHP-only grammar (LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) with HTML stripping
approaches.description: Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY and strip text outside <?php ... ?> before parsing, reusing approach A's queries.
pros: Pure-PHP grammar is smaller and has no text nodes to filter
Avoids ERROR-node risk from HTML mixed into the source
cons: Byte offsets and line numbers shift unless stripping preserves positions; this needs extra handling in the shared parser path
Changes shared parsing code outside the issue's scope
Fails the 'mixed HTML parses with zero ERROR nodes' criterion as written

recommendation: Approach A. Use LANGUAGE_PHP, populate ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_clause), DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance; leave the three receiver/function-name handlers None per the issue. Add 'php' to supported_languages() in lang.rs; without it the parser cache will reject PHP at runtime even though get_language_info succeeds. Prove the queries compile in a unit test before wiring the registry, as the issue suggests. Approach B is rejected because the acceptance criteria require inheritance and DEFUSE_QUERY; C is rejected because it changes the shared parse path and cannot meet the mixed-HTML criterion as written.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source: php/grammar.js is a 3-line stub calling common/define-grammar.js; the rules were read from common/define-grammar.js (lines 334-384) of tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php. Rules quoted: `class_declaration: $ => prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list)))`; `interface_declaration` has `optional($.base_clause)` before `field('body', $.declaration_list)`; `base_clause: $ => seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name))`; `class_interface_clause: $ => seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name))`; `_name` is choice(alias(keyword('static', false), $.name), alias(choice(...CAST_TYPE_CLASS_NAMES...), $.name), reserved('classes', $.name), $.qualified_name, $.relative_name). node-types.json (php/src/node-types.json) confirms class_declaration fields are only attributes, body, name (no superclass field), and base_clause / class_interface_clause have no fields, with children name | qualified_name | relative_name. Walk: for each named child c of the class_declaration node (no field lookup possible): if c.kind()=='base_clause' then for each named child n of c with kind in {name, qualified_name, relative_name} emit 'extends ' + source text of n; if c.kind()=='class_interface_clause' then for each named child n in {name, qualified_name, relative_name} emit 'implements ' + text of n. Same walk applies to interface_declaration (base_clause only; interfaces extend, so emit 'extends'). enum_declaration uses class_interface_clause only. trait_declaration has no inheritance clause. Qualified names keep backslashes (e.g. 'extends \\Bar\\Base'). Result order follows source order.
